prize_parts.citation: for discoveries of the physiology of glucagon-like peptide-1 and of its active form, which made incretin-based treatment of type 2 diabetes and obesity possible

statement.case_for: I keep a single-achievement prize for B040 with Drucker, Holst and Mojsov. The scientific chain is complete and independently confirmed: proglucagon processing, the active GLP-1(7-36) peptide and its glucose-dependent insulinotropic action in humans, receptor biology and appetite effects, and then large randomized outcome trials showing benefit for glycaemia, weight, cardiovascular and renal endpoints. The round-1 exchange did not weaken any of that; every stated reservation concerns attribution and framing, not the science or its maturity. Honouring the physiological discovery keeps the prize on discovery rather than on industrial drug design, and the three-person limit is respected by Holst (human physiology of the active peptide), Drucker (GLP-1 and GLP-2 biology, receptor action, translation) and Mojsov (identification and synthesis of the active form). I also do not want to rest this on the six-way opening first place, which the shortlist records but which is not evidence. A second part would force each part to a smaller share of three names and none of the candidate partners is, in my judgement, ripe and cleanly credited enough to justify that cost this year.
statement.case_against: The weakest point remains the exact trio. Mojsov's priority on the active peptide is contested, Habener-group work is outside the supplied names, and I cannot adjudicate the primary literature from the evidence given; my confidence in the field is higher than in the names. Excluding Knudsen is a real judgement that the discovery being honoured is the physiology and the active hormone, not the long-acting analogues, and critics could reasonably argue the opposite because liraglutide and semaglutide are what patients receive. If the committee were persuaded that analogue design was the decisive step, Knudsen would have to displace a physiology name, and I would then lean towards replacing Mojsov only if the primary record showed her contribution to be derivative, which I cannot establish. Long-term safety and durability of obesity effects are still being characterised, though this does not touch the discovery itself.

responses.point: B039 (unfolded protein response, Mori and Walter) is conceptually original, mechanistically complete and has the cleanest two-person credit on the shortlist, and you would keep Knudsen's analogue work out of a separate prize part.
responses.response: I agree with you on Knudsen: a separate analogue part would dilute a coherent story and would force a smaller share of the three names. I also accept that B039 is the strongest basic-science fallback and that the UPR is textbook biology. I still hold that its reach into patient outcomes is indirect, and Sandberg's point that Ron and Harding (PERK) and ATF6 contributors are outside the credited names means a Mori-Walter citation would have to be limited to the IRE1/HAC1/XBP1 arm. That is defensible but narrow, so I treat B039 as a candidate for a later year, not as a second part this year. I note we disagree on that timing and I do not claim support counts settle it.

responses.point: The imatinib case (B043) is clinically beyond doubt but the BCR-ABL oncogene discovery (Rowley and others) lies outside the credited trio, so you would frame it differently from my opening placement.
responses.response: You and Sandberg have persuaded me on framing. My opening record ranks B043 third, and I valued the concrete transformation of CML, but a prize to Druker, Lydon and Sawyers would honour validation of a principle whose discovery lineage is not credited, and I cannot repair that within three names. I keep my view that earlier recognition of adjacent work is not by itself a scientific objection, but the attribution gap is. I have therefore dropped B043 from my alternatives, and I also correct my round-1 text, which misstated my own imatinib rank; the shortlist record shows B043 third and B009 seventh.

responses.point: You moved to favour a narrower CAR-T pair (June and Sadelain) over your opening three-name proposal, and you rank CAR-T as the best second candidate behind GLP-1.
responses.response: I welcome the narrower pair, since Rosenberg's adoptive cell transfer and TIL work is a separate line from the engineered receptor. Eshhar's absence from the credited names is the larger gap and I do not think swapping names closes it. Against your view of CAR-T as a strong second part, I still see grounds for patience: efficacy is established in B-cell malignancies, but solid-tumour limits, toxicity and long-term safety are unresolved. So B034 stays my first alternative, as a configuration I would support in a later year or if B040 fails on attribution, but not as a pairing now.

responses.point: Optogenetics (B008) is a legitimate kind of prize and mature, but six credited names against a three-person limit means any trio leaves out someone decisive, and you separate the molecular channel discovery from the neuronal demonstration.
responses.response: I agree with your separation of the channelrhodopsin discovery (Nagel, Hegemann) from its neuronal deployment (Deisseroth), and that is the best available trio. But I accept your conclusion that Boyden, Bamberg and Miesenboeck are left out with strong claims, and I weigh that more heavily after reading your response. Medical translation in the retina is early. I keep B008 as my second alternative because the method is mature and transformative, not because I think the credit is resolved.

responses.point: If the committee judged drug design decisive, Knudsen would replace one of the three, but you would still keep her outside because the Nobel question is who discovered the hormone's actions; you also favour B039 as the fallback.
responses.response: I agree with your reasoning on the discovery being the object of the prize, and I accept your correction that my imatinib ranking was overstated as a discovery case. Where I qualify your view is on the cost of the exclusion: the citation should say that leaving out Knudsen and Habener reflects a choice about what was discovered, not a verdict on their importance. On B039 we differ on timing, as above, but I take your point that a Mori-Walter prize would implicitly rank the IRE1 arm over PERK.

uncertainties: Whether Mojsov's priority on the active peptide form, relative to the Habener group, is strong enough to hold a place; I cannot settle this from the supplied evidence.
Whether the committee will treat analogue design as decisive, in which case Knudsen would displace a physiology name and the configuration would change.
Whether a single-part prize is better than pairing B040 with a second part; I judge no partner (B034, B039, B008, B025) clean and ripe enough this year.
Long-term safety and durability of GLP-1 obesity therapy remain open, though they do not affect the discovery.
statement.conflict_note: No conflict requiring recusal. I disclose again about twenty co-authored works with Thomas Perlmann on dopamine neurons, Nurr1 and autophagy, and a postdoctoral period with Paul Greengard; none involves a credited name on B040, B034 or B008. Perlmann's preferred fallbacks (B039, B025) are not in my preferred configuration, so this relationship does not affect my position, and I note it for colleagues to weigh.
